$comment: Maintainer ruling 2026-09-12: Copilot supplies the sole automated review round. A separate APPROVED review is not required; the maintainer's human merge decision remains outside this automated readiness verdict. AUDITED 2026-09-18 -- this file is VALID at nen 0.10.0 and the empty default_approvers is DELIBERATE, said here rather than by omission, which is exactly what the loader demands. `approval_policy: "review-round-only"` is NOT inert: it is the key that makes the empty approval set legal, and it is load-bearing in both directions. Measured against the installed 0.10.0 binary: `nen schema check --repo .` reports `ok nen/gates.json`, and `nen pr ready <n> --gh-repo zheref/hatsu` evaluates normally (#76 -> not-ready, a reviewer round still owed at head). DELETE `approval_policy` and the same loader refuses: `at default_approvers, is empty. An empty approval set makes the approve limb of the readiness gate VACUOUSLY TRUE ...`. Set it to anything else and it refuses too: `at approval_policy, expected 'required' or 'review-round-only'`. A grep finding no consumer for `review-round-only` in a zheref/nen source tree means that CHECKOUT predates the feature -- it landed in nen 0.10.0 (nen #209, PR #210; release PR #211), which is why nen/contract.json raises `minimum` to 0.10. Check the checkout version before reading an absence as evidence. So: do not "fix" this file by populating default_approvers, and do not remove approval_policy as dead configuration. Doing either changes the readiness verdict for every Hatsu pull request.

reviewers.name: copilot
reviewers.$comment: Declared kind bot so that nen/workflow.json -> aiReviewers optional or off waives Copilot's round mechanically (zheref/hatsu#428). From nen 0.26, nen pr ready and nen pr merge --release-unit waive under optional or off only a reviewer declared kind bot with an IDENTICAL declaration in this file at the pull request's base and at the default branch's tip (nen src/gates/ai_reviewers.ts -> trustedBotReviewers compares the parsed identity: name, kind, patterns and options, never this $comment); an entry with no kind is unknown and its round binds. Without this key every Hatsu PR read 'aiReviewers optional waives bot rounds: (none)' and stopped at rounds-owed on a Copilot request GitHub never records (exit 9; HA-PR-#422 at ebd9be9f8, 2026-10-22). Read at the base, the key takes effect from the first PR whose base carries it, never on the PR that adds it (SEC-6). kind is nen's key (bot or human, from nen 0.24): never declare a human reviewer bot, since a bot's round is waivable. Once a change to this entry's reviewer keys merges, a PR whose base predates it gets no waiver until it catches up, because its base and the tip then differ. The rule is docs/PROCESS.md section AI reviewers per consumer; that a waived round reads ready is docs/ROSTER.md HR-333, ruled by the maintainer on 2026-10-22.

delivery.$comment: Current local delivery branches use the Codex prefix and the maintainer credentials.

checks.$comment: nen's key (from nen 0.20, zheref/nen#249), the home of a maintainer's ruling that a named check is not watched -- never a chat line, never a subagent brief, never a hand-passed --exclude-check. It replaces Hatsu's own check_exclusions key, retired by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-04, 'retire 2, adopt 2' (zheref/nen#310; zheref/hatsu#227; docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-04 -- retire 2, adopt 2). One entry per ruling: {"name": "<the check's rollup label, compared whole>", "match": "exact" or "glob" (required when name carries a *; a glob needs 3 literal characters before its first *), "reason": "<why>", "ruled": "<YYYY-MM-DD>", "until": "<YYYY-MM-DD>" or {"condition": "<what lifts it>"}}. nen pr ready and pr next-blocker read it AT THE PULL REQUEST'S BASE, never its head, so a PR cannot exempt its own red check (on a PR into main that base is the reviewed trunk; a stacked or integration base's file may not have passed main's gate, SEC-6); each honoured entry drops its checks from CON-32(a) and is named beside its reason; a dated entry lapses after its day, a condition entry is warned on at every evaluation until the file is edited, and a malformed entry is refused by pointer (nen schema check). The rule that reads the verdict is pr-state section 2's; the shape is docs/GATE-CONFIGURATION.md section 3. An empty list is a decision: nothing is excluded here.

round_quorum.$comment: nen's key (from nen 0.17): at least `minimum` of `any_of` must HAVE a round (a posted review or a SUCCESS round check, at any earlier head under bounded); once met it fulfils the owed round of an unavailable any_of member (no round-check run at head, a run that completed without a round, a pending review request with no round check), never one whose round-check run at head is still in flight -- the maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-29 (nen docs/USAGE.md section round_quorum), restated 2026-10-04: docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-04 -- one bot reviewer suffices; the behaviour is docs/PROCESS.md section Reviewer rounds and review threads, stated once. Every name must be a reviewers[] entry whose login_pattern, and any round_check_pattern it declares (optional: copilot above posts reviews and has none), is anchored to the bot's exact logins and check name (one member's round covers the others, so a broad pattern would let any matching login satisfy the whole group), so this group is Copilot alone until Cursor Bugbot is enrolled on zheref/hatsu as `bugbot` (its check reads skipping today), and that reviewers[] entry's round is excused once the quorum is met, from the v0.20.0 pin (zheref/nen#359/#361). This key is also what replaced Hatsu's reviewer_fallback, retired by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-04, 'retire 2, adopt 2' (zheref/nen#310, zheref/hatsu#227): an exhausted reviewer is no longer declared anywhere -- a met quorum fulfils its round.

round_policy.$comment: Maintainer's rulings of 2026-09-19 (zheref/hatsu#85) and the ceiling of zheref/hatsu#102 (#69's specification). All three fields are nen's: stallMinutes from nen 0.11.0, minRounds and maxRounds from nen 0.21.0 (zheref/nen#240), adopted under Hatsu's own names by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-04, 'retire 2, adopt 2' -- the one ruled exception to nen's same-name rule (nen docs/USAGE.md, Unknown keys are refused). stallMinutes: nen pr ready reads a pending review request older than it as not-ready: reviewer round stalled. maxRounds (M): nen pr request-reviews refuses a bot's request past it at exit 2 (refused: ... past the round_policy.maxRounds ceiling), reading it at the PR's base AND at the default branch's tip and applying the lower; a further round is a PR raising it, never a number raised in-session. minRounds (N): nen counts it against POSTED rounds and only labels pr ready --explain's per-reviewer counts (meta.roundCounts); Hatsu's skills count RESOLVED rounds against the same number (sharingan section 6 owns that rule: request only while requested < M AND resolved < N; once N resolved rounds exist no further round is requested -- 'owed at head' after the run's own push or request is not a reason; M with fewer than N resolved is the reported blocker, nen pr ready --explain quoted). Neither cap is a CON-32 conjunct: no readiness row, verdict or exit code moves on them. A key absent here takes contracts/round_policy.default.json's value in the skills (docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-09-30 -- reviewer-round caps by default); nen then enforces no ceiling. monitor.maxCycles in nen/workflow.json is a different number -- en's ACTING-cycle cap.
